summary: Standing 100-ft tower with 8x8 ft cab on Tunk Hill in Providence's Scituate watershed; built 1935 by the city, NHLR-registered 1992; visits by arranged group tour only.

access.note: Scituate Reservoir lands are closed to public entry; group tours can be arranged through the Providence Water Supply Board.

visit.trail_note: No public trail is described. Group tours can be arranged through the Providence Water Supply Board.

events.note: NHLR gives 1935 as the build year; the 1935 state annual report says the city had constructed the tower.
Earliest staffing found: the 1935 state report says the city maintains a watch at Tunk Hill. No crew details are given.
1952-53 state report: battery-operated sets were loaned to the Water Supply Board for use in the tower.
Registered August 6, 1992 as US 46, RI 1; nominated by the Providence Water Supply Board.

evidence.supports: built in 1935; 100-ft tower with 8x8 cab; active in watershed and state fire detection ever since
evidence.quote: Built in 1935, the 100-ft tower, with 8'x8' cab, has been active in watershed and state fire detection ever since.

evidence.supports: first registered lookout in RI and first registered municipally owned lookout; owned by City of Providence
evidence.quote: is the first lookout to be registered that is owned by a municipality, the City of Providence

evidence.supports: location in the Providence City Watershed
administered by the Providence Water Supply Board
Scituate lands closed to public entry; group tours by arrangement
evidence.quote: The Scituate Reservoir lands are closed to public entry, but arrangements can be made for group tours through the Providence Water Supply Board.

evidence.supports: 1935 state report: city constructed a tower and maintains a watch at Tunk Hill
evidence.quote: constructed a tower and maintains a watch at Tunk Hill

notes_for_editor: Two sources agree on the 1935 build. Staffing, notable fires and any later condition work are not in the sources read. Providence Water pages at provwater.com and the Providence Journal Scituate article (2026-09-30) returned HTTP 403 and may hold more history. The register's 'active ever since' wording is general. Brief access 'unknown' is now resolved to permission-only by the NHLR text. No corrections to the brief.
